ukmt-pink-2020-01.title: Count the outside edges
ukmt-pink-2020-01.body:
Each square has 4 sides, giving $10\times4=40$ sides. Each pair of squares that share an edge hides 2 of these. In the shape there are 7 side-by-side pairs (1 in the top row, 5 in the middle row, 1 in the bottom row) and 4 pairs one above the other, so 11 shared edges. The perimeter is $40-2\times11=18$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 18**

ukmt-pink-2020-01.title: Walk round the outline
ukmt-pink-2020-01.body:
Count the unit edges along the boundary: tracing the outline of the figure gives 18 unit edges, so the perimeter is 18 cm.

**Answer: (B) 18**

ukmt-pink-2020-08.title: Use the signposts
ukmt-pink-2020-08.body:
The first sign shows that Atown is 3 km behind and Betown is 1 km ahead, so Atown to Betown is $3+1=4$ km. The second sign is 6 km from Atown, so it is $6-4=2$ km from Betown.

**Answer: (A) 2 km**

ukmt-pink-2020-11.title: Make 20 times the number square
ukmt-pink-2020-11.body:
The numbers are $20ab$ and the product is $20\times ab$ where $ab$ is a two-digit number from 10 to 99. Since $20=2^2\times5$, the product is a square exactly when $ab=5k^2$ for some integer $k$. In the range 10 to 99: $5\times4=20$, $5\times9=45$, $5\times16=80$ (and $5\times1=5$, $5\times25=125$ are out of range).

So the numbers are 2020, 2045 and 2080: three of them.

**Answer: (C) 3**

ukmt-pink-2020-16.title: Divisibility by 18
ukmt-pink-2020-16.body:
A number is divisible by 18 when it is divisible by 2 and by 9. The digit sum is $1+2+\dots+9=45$, so every arrangement is divisible by 9. So the number is divisible by 18 exactly when it is even, i.e. its last digit is 2, 4, 6 or 8. By symmetry each digit is equally likely to be last, so the probability is $\frac49$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac49$**

ukmt-pink-2020-20.title: Find the apex label
ukmt-pink-2020-20.body:
Let $x$ be the label at the apex. The square face has the other four labels, so its sum is $15-x\ge10$. If the square were one of the four given sums, it would be 10 and $x=5$. Then the face with sum 7 would be a triangle face containing the apex 5, but such a face has sum at least $5+1+2=8$, a contradiction. So the square is not among the given faces, and the four triangular faces have sums $7,8,9,10$, total 34.

Each triangular face contains the apex, and each base vertex lies in exactly two triangular faces. So the four triangle sums add to $4x+2(15-x)=2x+30$. Hence $2x+30=34$, $x=2$, and the square face has sum $15-2=13$.

**Answer: (C) 13**

ukmt-pink-2020-24.title: Use the least common multiple
ukmt-pink-2020-24.body:
No number can end in 0, since it would have to be divisible by 0. Among eight consecutive integers the last digits are therefore $1,2,\dots,8$ or $2,3,\dots,9$, in order. Write the numbers as $\overline{AB}n$. Divisibility of $\overline{AB}n$ by $n$ is the same as divisibility of $\overline{AB}0$ by $n$, since $\overline{AB}n=\overline{AB}0+n$.

If the last digits are $2,\dots,9$, then $\overline{AB}0$ must be a multiple of $\text{lcm}(2,\dots,9)=2520$, which is impossible for a three-digit number. So the last digits are $1,\dots,8$ and $\overline{AB}0$ is a multiple of $\text{lcm}(1,\dots,8)=840$. The only three-digit multiple is 840, so the numbers are $841,842,\dots,848$.

The smallest is 841, with digit sum $8+4+1=13$.

**Answer: (E) 13**
